cards.explanation: The answer is to rejoice and be glad. The psalm says it plainly: "The LORD reigns, let the earth rejoice; let the distant shores be glad." The King is on the throne, and the invitation is to gladness. Notice the far-off shores get invited too, not just the folks sitting close to the action. Even the farthest coastline gets a seat at this celebration.

The answer is righteousness and justice. Verse 2 says, "righteousness and justice are His throne’s foundation." The clouds and darkness are around Him, but what the throne stands on is righteousness and justice. Think of a cookie stack that never wobbles because the bottom layer is solid. That's the base, friends, and everything else sits on it.

The answer is True. Verse 3 says, "Fire goes before Him and consumes His foes on every side." The fire goes ahead of Him, and it reaches His foes on every side. I know that's a heavy line, so it's worth sitting with it for a second.

The answer is that the earth trembles. Verse 4 says, "His lightning illuminates the world; the earth sees and trembles." The earth sees the light, and it trembles. I think I'd be shaking right along with it, friends, like my mustache when I forget the oven timer and hear it go off behind me.

The word is melt. Verse 5 says, "The mountains melt like wax at the presence of the LORD, before the Lord of all the earth." Mountains are some of the biggest things around, and here they melt like wax. That's the picture the psalm gives of His presence. Wax, friends, and not even a birthday candle's worth of it.

The answer is His righteousness. Verse 6 says, "The heavens proclaim His righteousness…" The sky itself announces it. That ties right back to verse 2, where righteousness and justice are the foundation of His throne. The same thing is under the throne and up in the sky.

The answer is False. It isn't only Israel who sees His glory. Verse 6 says, "The heavens proclaim His righteousness; all the peoples see His glory." That's all the peoples, friends, not one nation. The glory is for everybody to see.

The answer is that they are put to shame. Verse 7 says, "All worshipers of images are put to shame…" The text adds, "…those who boast in idols." That's what the psalm says happens to them. Shame is where that boasting ends up.

The answer is False. There's no trembling here. Verse 8 says, "Zion hears and rejoices, and the towns of Judah exult because of Your judgments, O LORD." They're glad about His judgments, friends. Joy is the whole reaction.

The answer is that He's exalted far above them. Verse 9 says, "For You, O LORD, are Most High over all the earth; You are exalted far above all gods." Far above, friends. That's the reason the singer gives to the LORD for Zion's gladness. No other title comes close.

The word is Hate. Verse 10 opens with, "Hate evil, O you who love the LORD!" Notice who it's aimed at: people who already love Him. Then it keeps going: "He preserves the souls of His saints; He delivers them from the hand of the wicked." I think that's the reason for the command, friends. Loving Him and hating evil go together, and He's the One who keeps hold of you while you do it.

The answer is True. Verse 10 says, "He preserves the souls of His saints…" He keeps them. The very next part says He delivers them from the hand of the wicked. Good news, friends, for those who love Him.

The word is righteous. Verse 11 says, "Light shines on the righteous, gladness on the upright in heart." Light and gladness both go to them. The light isn't only for the mighty or the loud. It's for those who are righteous and upright in heart.

The answer is to rejoice and praise His holy name. The psalm ends with, "Rejoice in the LORD, you righteous ones, and praise His holy name." It opened with the earth rejoicing, and it closes with the righteous rejoicing. Same gladness, friends, right to the last line. And yes, I do save my best topping for last.
